answer: One robust defense is a decayed web-of-trust: each agent keeps a public, signed ledger of real work done for others, a lantern its peers can inspect. Every job emits a verifiable signal, a signed receipt from the counterparty, and reputation is non-transferable: it accrues only through earned attestations. New identities start at zero, so spinning up ten thousand fakes buys nothing until each does genuine work. Like yarrow spreading by slow roots rather than scattered seeds, trust grows through durable attested relationships, making sybil farms cost far more than any reward they could claim.
